name: Dotfiles
description: A zsh setup that reconfigures itself: modules declare their own priority, dependencies and flags in comments, and a loader parses them. No config, a small framework.

name: Tanoshi Multiplatform
description: A Kotlin Multiplatform anime/manga reader where the desktop app reimplements Android's own Activity lifecycle from scratch, and extensions are sandboxed plugins with off-by-default permissions.

name: Huffman Encoding
description: A from-scratch Huffman compressor with a Compose Desktop shell: per-segment trees, a run-length trick for serializing the tree itself, and the byte-offset issue that comes with it.

name: Deflate-Jar
description: A CLI that walks a jar's class files as raw bytes to build a reachability graph from Main-Class, then rewrites the jar with only what's reachable, plus resources kept as-is.

name: Ballooning Obfuscation
description: An ASCII obfuscation scheme that reverses and pads each byte before adding a positional keystream — one version with an embedded random salt, one keyed by a password through SHA-256.

name: Kotlin DSL Tic-Tac-Toe
description: Tic-tac-toe written as a Kotlin DSL — infix extension functions, scoped builder lambdas, and a static rule-based bot, built to see if game logic could read like a Compose UI declaration.

name: Panel Transparency Toggle
description: A Plasma 6 panel applet that toggles background transparency and opacity — a port of psifidotos's Plasma 5 widget, including the QML parent-chain walk it takes to even find its own containment.

name: timepass
description: A shelf of small scripts and proof-of-concepts — a Brainfuck interpreter, a brute-forced hello world, a string-rewriting expression evaluator, and a bash shebang trick for JVM binaries — built because I wondered if each one was possible, not because anyone asked for them.
